I've been having a hell of a time trying to create a recovery stick for my daughter's new Dell laptop. It will start to do create the recovery media and then fail out. Now I'm assuming I can download one of these ISOs and be good to go, but I've also found that there doesn't seem to be a Windows 10 product key anywhere. Is this embedded in the BIOS/UEFI somewhere or do I need to go spelunking under the battery or something? Or, is there a program that will search for the key if it's hidden somewhere in the system? She just got it a few days ago so I'm not too worried about it failing any time soon, but if it does, or I upgrade her drive in the future, I'd kinda like to be able to have a painless reinstall. Any guidance would be greatly appreciated.

Download the standalone version of Speccy:

http://www.piriform.com/speccy/builds

It is a Zip file. Once you have downloaded and extracted it, run the proper version (32 or 64bit, most likely 64) then it will detect your hardware, etc. Click on "Operating System" and it will give you your serial number.

I just ran it on my Windows 10 machine and it worked fine.

There is also this utility:

http://www.nirsoft.net/utils/product_cd_key_viewer.html

I ran it waaaay back in the XP days. I believe you are correct though in that the serial numbers are embedded within the system firmware by the OEMs now. Very handy indeed. So really, I don't think you have anything to worry about. I would just go about creating a bootable USB drive with the Windows 10 ISO and perform the upgrade.
